label: M2 money supply
description: Broad money supply (M3) — the total amount of money in the Australian economy, including physical currency, bank deposits, and other liquid assets. Measured in billions of dollars.
explainer: Money supply measures how much money is circulating in the economy. When the money supply grows faster than the economy, inflation typically follows — you can see this relationship clearly by overlaying M2 with CPI. The RBA influences money supply through interest rates and, during Covid, through quantitative easing (bond purchases). M2 more than doubled between 2009 and 2023.
projection_source: RBA monetary policy projections. Growth assumed to moderate in line with credit growth forecasts.
